PullRequest.Title: chat: preserve Markdown continuity across empty thinking

Keep streamed Markdown continuous across empty thinking markers, including replay, copying, accessible text, and Find. Preserve reasoning markers, real content boundaries, and subagent file references without dropping recorded deltas.

Fixes #343322.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: Both synchronous call paths and the lack of memoization are explicit in the code. getLegacySubagentMarkdown's guard limits substantial work to responses containing a non-standalone subagent codeblockUri; for those responses it constructs and lexes the full Markdown. The uncertain factors are the size and prevalence of these restored histories, not the additional pass.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU spent rebuilding normalization text, lexing Markdown, and scanning source/removal spans, plus temporary strings, arrays, and lexer tokens.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: One additional normalization per qualifying response per completed query/content debounce, across the entire transcript. Work scales with each response's full Markdown and source-span/removal collections; cold and warm rebuilds both repeat it. It is not a separate operation per file reference.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased synchronous Find-rebuild latency and allocation/GC pressure on large restored transcripts.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Find performed one legacy-normalization pass per response for annotation/source mapping, then extracted plaintext directly from the raw parts. Accessible View likewise performed its existing annotation pass for joined code-block descriptions without independently rerunning legacy normalization during its parts loop.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Plaintext extraction independently repeats legacy normalization after its caller has already performed it for rendered-part mapping. The Accessible View provider also already normalizes through describeJoinedCodeBlocks before entering this new generator.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added chatModel.ts:3988 invokes getLegacySubagentMarkdown from getResponsePartsForPlaintext. The changed chatFindContent.ts:100 now uses this generator, whereas the old loop visited response parts directly. chatFindModel.ts:74 already invokes annotateSpecialMarkdownContentWithSource, whose annotations.ts:23 calls the same normalization helper. Thus each Find rebuild now normalizes every qualifying response twice instead of once.
Findings.Title: Share legacy normalization with plaintext extraction
Findings.Impact: Searching a large restored agent transcript with legacy subagent file references performs an extra full-response Markdown lexing/allocation pass for every qualifying response on each debounced rebuild, increasing main-thread pauses and GC pressure. This also applies when those responses contain no empty thinking markers.
Findings.Evidence: chatFindModel.ts:74 computes annotations before calling getChatFindTextParts at line 84. annotations.ts:23 normalizes through getLegacySubagentMarkdown. The new generator repeats that call at chatModel.ts:3988. For qualifying responses, chatModel.ts:4035-4114 builds concatenated text and span arrays, invokes marked.lexer for each segment, and computes removals. None of these results are cached. ChatFindModel.recompute builds segments for the entire transcript synchronously; chatFindWidget.ts:258,311-320 coalesces content changes with a 200 ms Delayer but does not reuse normalization between the two calls within one rebuild. Accessible View similarly calls describeJoinedCodeBlocks, which annotates, before iterating the generator.
Findings.Recommendation: Compute legacy normalization once per response extraction/rebuild and pass the result to both annotation and plaintext coalescing. Keep the existing distinct plaintext/source-mapping semantics; a persistent cache is not necessary to eliminate this duplicate pass.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Copying the accumulated sourceIndexes array for each merged fragment caused quadratic index copying and temporary allocations.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Avoidable synchronous CPU and GC pressure on fragmented restored responses and inline-reference runs; established statically, without measured timings.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: Push source indices into function-local arrays, eliminating repeated growing-array copies while preserving source mappings.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Base annotations.ts:94 spread the entire growing sourceIndexes array for every compatible Markdown merge. A run of n compatible restored fragments therefore copied n(n-1)/2 indices. The annotation function is synchronously called by chatListRenderer.ts:getNextProgressiveRenderContent and chatFindModel.ts:buildSegments. Added annotations.ts:89 uses push on the locally owned entry instead, and analogous merge branches are updated. blame_base_line resolved the old allocation to f5929d2a1e34b2dc062e80f9b14958d915928a44 at the same origin path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Stream an ordinary text response across empty thinking markers and update working progress.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Response.updateContent synchronously updates model parts and invalidates text caches; subsequent renderer passes annotate and diff content before displaying it. The working-indicator change preserves the existing delay after Markdown.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Markdown deltas, accumulated response parts, retained empty markers, and total displayed characters. Markers were retained before this PR as well.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Model updates and annotation run serially on the renderer thread. Progressive rendering schedules/coalesces presentation; the optional incremental morpher uses animation frames and is disabled by default.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Response.toString/getMarkdown cache their results until _contentChanged invalidates them. Rendered parts and optional morpher are reused. The new hasFollowingMarkdown flag is set once per crossed marker; no new long-lived collection is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced updateContent, cache invalidation, annotation, progressive content construction, content diffing, and empty-marker rendering. Plain text in this scenario introduces no filesystem, subprocess, IPC, database, or network call.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider marker frequency and response length vary. No timing measurements were collected.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding for continuity/progress changes. Extra model scanning was considered against existing whole-parts filtering; marker retention is pre-existing. The required Markdown joining is not by itself evidence of an avoidable regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Reopen a local session containing fragmented Markdown and legacy subagent file-reference scaffolding.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A cold open awaits session-file reading and reconstructs the operation log/JSON before creating the model. Annotation then normalizes legacy scaffolding and constructs renderable parts/source mappings.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the selected session log, or fall back to its flat JSON file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally one successful file read per cold session load; an unavailable log adds the existing fallback read. Warm acquired models avoid this path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same session-level read, fallback behavior, and storeQueue existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Session data must be available before model restoration and rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Parse log entries or flat JSON and revive response data.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One reconstruction per cold load, proportional to stored entries and bytes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same deserialization path processed recorded response parts before the PR.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Normalize legacy Markdown and merge compatible source parts for rendering.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One normalization per annotation invocation; full Markdown lexing is guarded by the presence of a non-standalone subagent codeblockUri.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Normalization already existed. Source-index accumulation previously allocated and copied the growing index array on each merge; the PR now pushes into a locally owned array.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously before annotated content is consumed.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected session file, its log entries, response parts and characters, and the number of source fragments merged into each annotated Markdown block.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Session reads use the existing global storeQueue. Log reconstruction and annotation are synchronous. There is no filesystem call per marker or file-reference annotation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: An already acquired model bypasses session-file loading. Cold loading tries the log first and falls back to the flat file if unavailable; those existing fallback reads are unchanged. Annotation results are reconstructed per invocation rather than persistently cached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced cold/warm acquisition, queued session reads, replay, and annotation. Base blame identifies the introducing commit for the removed quadratic source-index copying.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Restored history fragmentation and byte size vary; improvements and costs were established statically rather than measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: No new loading-boundary fan-out found. Recorded one internal regression-fix signal for eliminating quadratic sourceIndexes copying; this is not a finding against the PR.

Scenarios.Scenario: Copy a response or Copy Final Response across empty thinking markers.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The selected action synchronously builds the requested string. getFinalResponse now crosses empty markers when identifying the final Markdown run.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Characters and parts in the selected response/final contiguous run, not the entire session.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous traversal/string construction; no task fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The general string representation is lazy and cached until content changes. getFinalResponse remains uncached. Legacy normalization in the general representation was already present.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: inspected AbstractResponse.getFinalResponse, partsToRepr, and cache invalidation. These helpers do not perform subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Copied response size varies. This analysis covers string extraction; downstream clipboard handling is unchanged by the diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No independent performance regression. Traversing the additional fragments is necessary to return the requested complete text and does not add a repeated external boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Find within a large restored transcript containing legacy subagent file references, including responses without empty thinking markers.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each nonempty-query recomputation synchronously builds segments for the entire transcript before producing matches. buildSegments first annotates each response, then calls plaintext extraction. Both now independently normalize the same response.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Build full-response normalization text/spans and lex Markdown to remove legacy subagent scaffolding.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Previously once per qualifying response per Find rebuild; now twice, once through annotation and once through the added generator.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Annotation performed the normalization once; the old plaintext extractor directly iterated raw response parts and did not invoke it again.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both passes block segment construction and match publication on the main thread.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Parse and sanitize searchable Markdown as plaintext.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per extracted Markdown run; coalescing can reduce the number of runs. renderAsPlaintext has its existing 100,000-character cap, which does not bound the preceding legacy-normalization passes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Plaintext parsing/sanitization already occurred for each raw Markdown part.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: All transcript responses; substantial duplicate work is limited to responses with a non-standalone subagent codeblockUri. Within those responses, work scales with full Markdown bytes and source/removal spans, not with one external call per referenced file.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serial renderer-thread processing. Query changes are debounced and content changes use a 200 ms Delayer, but the two normalization calls occur sequentially within each completed rebuild. No worker offloading or shared normalization exists.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No normalization cache or response-version reuse, even for completed responses. Cold and warm searches both recompute it. Responses without qualifying legacy metadata take the helper's inexpensive early return.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: explicit added helper call and both caller chains prove the duplicate normalization; debounce and the qualifying-metadata guard were accounted for.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The size/prevalence of affected older histories and the absolute pause duration are unmeasured. Already-coalesced large responses can incur the extra full parse without benefiting from fewer plaintext runs.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported one medium-severity repeated-work regression, anchored to the new normalization call. The bounded correction is to share one authoritative normalization result within each extraction/rebuild.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or refresh Accessible View for a response, including native visual descriptions.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: provideContent synchronously extracts and joins plaintext for the focused response. Its existing describeJoinedCodeBlocks path annotates the response before the new plaintext generator repeats normalization.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Normalize legacy Markdown while annotating joined code blocks, then independently normalize it again for plaintext coalescing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: For provider calls with the code-block describer, two normalizations of the focused qualifying response instead of the previous one.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing joined-code-block annotation performed normalization; the following raw-parts loop did not repeat it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both passes run before accessible content can be returned.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Parse/sanitize Markdown and obtain text descriptions for native visual code blocks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing joined-run and separate-source checks plus extracted Markdown runs; coalescing changes grouping but introduces no service/network fetch in the inspected extraction code.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Joined-code-block description and plaintext parsing were already performed.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Only the focused response, its full Markdown, source fragments, native code blocks, and tool descriptions. This is not a pass over the entire transcript.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous provider extraction. The provider emits changes when its focused model changes; no parallel normalization or per-reference external requests are introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The provider does not cache normalization between its joined-code-block pass and plaintext extraction. Settings are read from the existing storage service; subscriptions are disposed through existing ownership.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the duplicated normalization and provider reachability. Native description rendering remains the existing path rather than a new external boundary.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Response size and Accessible View refresh frequency vary; no runtime duration measurements were made.
Scenarios.Verdict: Same root cause as the Find finding, not a separate finding. No new retained subscription or external-call fan-out identified.

Scenarios.Scenario: Persist live local sessions and replay their recorded deltas.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing storage save events enqueue session persistence. Display does not await disk writes; model disposal and shutdown can wait for persistence. Serialization itself runs synchronously when the queued save executes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Clone serializable response parts, compute positional mutations, and encode JSON log entries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One extraction/diff per selected session per queued save. A changed earlier merged Markdown slot can move the suffix rewrite earlier; there is no per-delta production save introduced by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same whole-part extraction and positional-suffix mutation mechanism existed. Empty markers previously separated Markdown slots; normal streamed Markdown already updated merged slots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous CPU/allocation during the queued task, before its disk write; normal response streaming does not await completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Append or replace the session log, followed by existing batch index maintenance.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one session-log write with nonempty mutation data per selected session per save batch; existing index work follows the batch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same session-level write count, append/replace handling, global batch queue, and within-batch concurrency existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the normal chat-display dependency chain, but awaited by the save task and relevant disposal/shutdown paths.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Live local sessions in a save batch, response parts/bytes, and operation-log entries. Saves are normally coalesced by the storage service's minute interval, not performed once per streamed delta.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A global storeQueue serializes save batches; within a batch Promise.all writes the selected sessions. The PR adds no new saver, queue, subprocess, or per-marker filesystem operation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The serializer compares with the last confirmed persisted snapshot; failed writes are not confirmed. Cold persistence writes an initial state, warm persistence appends mutations, and the existing 1024-entry compaction threshold rewrites the log. Merged Markdown changes which positional suffix is represented in mutations.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for serializer behavior and actual save cadence/concurrency; no assumption of per-token persistence was used.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Mutation sizes depend on marker density, generation duration across minute-spaced saves, and position of edited parts. No measured independently material persistence degradation was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding for persistence. The diff changes recorded part shapes and preserves deltas, but does not introduce save-frequency or boundary-call fan-out. Considered existing positional suffix rewriting in the before/after comparison.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all 12 changed files and all diff pages against base c7a4394a0f142e03dbf838c7d95722b4154d26af. Submitted one finding for duplicate synchronous legacy normalization in Find/Accessible View. Recorded one internal regression fix with blame provenance for quadratic source-index array copying. Reviewed streaming, rendering/annotation, copy, restoration, accessibility, Find, and persistence scenarios; analysis is static and makes no benchmark claims.
